story: James J. Hill built the bridge in 1882 and 1883 for his railroad, the St. Paul, Minneapolis and Manitoba, which became the Great Northern Railway. Charles C. Smith designed it.
It is about 2,100 feet long, with granite piers from Sauk Rapids and limestone upper sections. It carried trains to the Great Northern Depot.
The Minneapolis Park Board converted it to a bike and walking path in 1994. It was named a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark in 1974.
stops.disputed: Counts of its arches vary by source, since one span is steel. Treat any number you read as approximate.

claims.t: The Stone Arch Bridge was built in the 1880s.
The Stone Arch Bridge was built for cars.
claims.why: It was built as a railroad bridge.

story: The Washburn A Mill was built in 1874 and was called the largest flour mill in the world. On May 2, 1878, airborne flour dust ignited. The explosion killed 14 workers instantly and four more died in the fire. Five other mills were destroyed.
Afterward, mills across the country added ventilation and other safety devices. William de la Barre designed a new Washburn A Mill, which opened in 1880 as the world's largest flour mill until 1881.
A fire in 1991 nearly destroyed the old mill. The Minnesota Historical Society opened the Mill City Museum in 2003, with a Flour Tower freight-elevator exhibit that feels like a working mill.
stops.disputed: The final death count is usually given as 18. Some counts treat the later deaths separately.

claims.t: Flour dust caused the 1878 mill explosion.
The Washburn A Mill was never rebuilt after 1878.
claims.why: A new Washburn A Mill opened in 1880.

stops.name: Saint Anthony Falls
stops.teaser: The only big waterfall on the Mississippi, and the reason there was a mill city.
stops.clue: Walk to the river just upstream of the Stone Arch Bridge, where the water drops over a wide apron beside the old mills.
stops.safety: Stay behind railings and on marked paths. Do not climb on the apron or lock walls. Wet stone is slippery.

story: Saint Anthony Falls was the only natural major waterfall on the Mississippi River. Father Louis Hennepin named it in 1680 after St. Anthony of Padua. The Dakota name is Owámniyomni, meaning whirlpool.

The total drop is 49 feet. The natural falls were about 35 feet and the upper dam adds about 14. On October 5, 1869, the limestone cap was breached during a tunnel project, and a concrete dike finished in 1876 fixed the damage. An Army Corps of Engineers wooden apron went in around 1880 and was replaced with concrete after it was destroyed in 1952.

Water power ran flour and lumber mills, and Minneapolis was known as the Flour Milling Capital of the World from about 1880 to 1930. The locks were completed in 1963. The upper lock was permanently closed in 2015 to help stop the spread of Asian carp.
stops.fact: The upper lock was closed in 2015 to stop Asian carp.
stops.disputed: Wikipedia says the falls was the only natural major waterfall, so some sources call it the only waterfall on the river. The natural falls no longer look natural, because the apron and dam changed them.

claims.t: Saint Anthony Falls was named in 1680.
claims.why: Wikipedia: Father Louis Hennepin named it in 1680.

claims.t: The falls you see today are completely natural.
claims.why: A concrete apron, dike and dam control the water.

story: The Basilica of Saint Mary was designated a minor basilica by Pope Pius XI in 1926, the first in the United States. Emmanuel Masqueray was the architect. Construction ran from 1907 to 1914, and the first Mass was held on May 31, 1914.
The sanctuary dome rises 138 feet above the floor. With the flèche and cross it reaches 200 feet. The nave is lit by five large arched stained glass windows, and the pews hold 1,600 people.
The style is Classical Revival, and the history section calls it Beaux-Arts. It stands at 1600 Hennepin Avenue between 16th and 17th Streets.
stops.disputed: Wikipedia gives two dedication dates, 1913 in the lead and 1921 in the history section, and does not reconcile them. Check a church source before repeating one.

claims.t: The Basilica of Saint Mary was the first basilica in the United States.
claims.why: Wikipedia: designated by Pope Pius XI in 1926.
Construction began in 1907. The first Mass was on May 31, 1914.
